ai.literal: That which will be lost, and that which will be gained, and the profit that will yield in the future, having pondered, one should act.
ai.translation: Weigh the loss, the gain, and the ultimate profit that will follow in the future, and then undertake the action.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலைச் செய்யும்போது அதனால் அழியும் பொருள், உண்டாகும் பொருள், பின்னர் அது தரும் லாபம் ஆகியவற்றை ஆராய்ந்து செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: Before undertaking any action, one must carefully calculate three things: the immediate loss or expenditure involved (அழிவதூஉம்), the immediate gain or result (ஆவதூஉம்), and the lasting benefit or profit that will accrue in the long run (வழிபயக்கும் ஊதியமும்). Only after thoroughly deliberating on these three aspects should one proceed with the task. This ensures that the effort is not wasted and leads to sustainable success.

ai.literal: To those who do [things] after deliberating with chosen associates and planning [carefully], there is not even one difficult matter.
ai.translation: For those who act after consulting with chosen associates and deliberating deeply, there is no task too difficult to achieve.
ai.modern: ஆராய்ந்து தேர்ந்தெடுக்கப்பட்ட நண்பர்களுடன் ஆலோசித்து, செயலைப்பற்றி நன்கு சிந்தித்துச் செயல்படுபவர்களுக்கு, செய்வதற்கு அரிய செயல் என்று ஒன்றுமே இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the power of collective deliberation and thorough planning before undertaking any action. The phrase 'தெரிந்த இனத்தொடு' refers to wise, reliable associates who have been carefully chosen for their counsel. 'தேர்ந்து எண்ணி' highlights the process of analyzing and planning the course of action in consultation with them. For those who proceed with such meticulous preparation, the poet declares that there is no 'அரும்பொருள்' (difficult task or rare achievement) that remains impossible ('யாதொன்றும் இல்').

ai.literal: Gain aiming at, capital losing action, will not undertake those who possess wisdom.
ai.translation: Those who possess wisdom will not undertake an action that risks losing their existing capital in the pursuit of profit.
ai.modern: இலாபத்தை எதிர்பார்த்து, முதலீட்டையே இழக்கச் செய்யும் செயலை அறிவுடையவர்கள் செய்யத் தொடங்க மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises on the importance of risk assessment before starting any venture. The word 'ākkam' refers to the expected profit or growth, while 'mutal' refers to the base capital or existing assets. Wise people ('aṟivuṭaiyār') will not be motivated ('ūkkār') to initiate an action ('ceyviṉai') if a careful analysis reveals that the pursuit of extra gain might end up destroying the very foundation of what they already own. Preserving one's core resources is prioritized over speculative and highly risky gains.

ai.literal: Clarity lacking that [action] they will not begin, disgrace which is called ruin fearing-those.
ai.translation: Those who fear the ruin called disgrace will not embark on any action that lacks clarity.
ai.modern: அவமானம் என்னும் துன்பத்திற்கு அஞ்சுகின்றவர்கள், தெளிவில்லாத செயலைத் தொடங்க மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of clarity and foresight before initiating any task. Those who are deeply concerned about their reputation and dread the ruin brought by disgrace (இளிவு) will never start an action without complete certainty (தெளிவு). The word 'ஏதப்பாடு' refers to the state of affliction or ruin that results from failure. By ensuring thorough clarity beforehand, one guards against the shame of an unsuccessful venture.

ai.literal: Without completely deliberating the means, rising up to act is a way of planting enemies in a garden bed.
ai.translation: To launch an action without thoroughly planning the means is a way of planting one's enemies in a fertile garden bed, helping them grow strong.
ai.modern: செயல் செய்யும் வழிகளை முழுமையாக ஆராயாமல் செயலில் இறங்குவது, பகைவர்களைப் பாத்தியில் நட்டு வளர்ப்பதற்கு ஒப்பான ஒரு வழியாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against acting without a complete and detailed plan. The phrase 'vakaiyaṟa cūḻātu' means failing to deliberate thoroughly on all the possible ways and means of executing an action. If a person rushes into action or war without such planning, they are not defeating their enemies; instead, they are doing something that benefits them. The poet uses the agricultural metaphor of 'pātti' (a garden bed) to show that unplanned action is like preparing a fertile plot of land to plant and nurture one's own enemies, allowing them to take root and flourish.

ai.literal: By doing those things which are not fit to be done, one will be ruined; by not doing those things which are fit to be done, one will also be ruined.
ai.translation: One is ruined by doing what ought not to be done; one is also ruined by failing to do what ought to be done.
ai.modern: செய்யத்தகாத செயல்களைச் செய்வதனாலும் ஒருவன் அழிவான்; செய்யத்தக்க செயல்களைச் செய்யாமல் விடுவதனாலும் அவன் அழிவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains that ruin comes from two types of errors: commission and omission. The first line states that performing actions that are improper or unfit (cey-takka alla) leads to destruction. The second line warns that failing to perform actions that are necessary and proper (cey-takka) also leads to the exact same ruin. A wise person must therefore balance action and inaction, knowing both what to avoid and what to execute.

ai.literal: Having deliberated, resolve on an action; after resolving, saying 'we will think' is a fault.
ai.translation: Deliberate deeply before undertaking an action; to say 'we will think about it' after having resolved to start is a grave error.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலை நன்றாக ஆராய்ந்து பின்னரே அதில் ஈடுபட வேண்டும்; ஈடுபட்ட பிறகு 'ஆராய்ந்து கொள்ளலாம்' என்று நினைப்பது குற்றமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of thorough planning before embarking on any task. The poet advises that one should think deeply and weigh all consequences before committing to an action. Once the decision is made and the action is initiated, hesitating or saying 'we will think about it later' is a serious flaw that leads to failure. The contrast between thinking before acting and thinking after acting highlights that timing is crucial in decision-making.

ai.literal: By the proper method not strived-for undertaking, many standing even if they guard, ruined with holes will become.
ai.translation: An undertaking that is not carried out through the proper method will fail and fall to pieces, even if many people stand together to guard and support it.
ai.modern: முறையான வழியில் முயற்சி செய்யாத ஒரு செயலை, பலர் ஒன்று கூடிப் பாதுகாத்தாலும் அது தோல்வியடைந்து அழியும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that the correct method (ஆறு) is essential for the success of any undertaking. An effort (வருத்தம்) that is not executed through the right systematic path (ஆற்றின் வருந்தா) is fundamentally flawed. Even if a large group of people stand together (பலர் நின்று) to protect and support it (போற்றினும்), the project will eventually develop leaks and collapse (பொத்துப்படும்). Success depends entirely on the soundness of the plan and method, not on the sheer number of supporters trying to save a flawed execution.

ai.literal: Even within doing good, there is mistake, if [one] does not do [it] having known each person's nature.
ai.translation: Even in doing good, failure can occur if one does not act after understanding the specific nature of the individuals involved.
ai.modern: ஒவ்வொருவருடைய குணத்தையும் அறிந்து அதற்கேற்பச் செய்யாவிட்டால், நன்மை செய்வதிலும் தவறு நேர்ந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns that even well-intentioned actions can go wrong and result in failure. Doing good is not enough on its own; one must understand the unique character and temperament of the person receiving the help or involved in the action. If we act without this understanding, the good deed may backfire, turn into a mistake, or cause unintended harm. Therefore, thoughtful action requires analyzing both the deed and the nature of the people affected by it.

ai.literal: Actions not despised, having deliberated, one must do; things that do not fit with oneself, the world will not accept.
ai.translation: One must deliberate and perform only those actions that are not despised by others; for the world will not accept actions that do not fit one's own character or position.
ai.modern: பிறரால் இகழப்படாத செயல்களை ஆராய்ந்து செய்ய வேண்டும்; தன் நிலைக்குப் பொருந்தாத செயல்களை உலகம் ஏற்றுக்கொள்ளாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of careful deliberation before acting, focusing on social acceptance and personal alignment. The author advises that any action undertaken must be blameless and free from the scorn of the wise. Furthermore, the action must align with one's own capacity, character, and position. If a person attempts something that is incompatible with their true nature or status, society will reject it and will not support them. Thus, successful action requires both public approval and personal compatibility.
